chu_de: Why is Greenland part of Denmark?

cau.chu: This island is eighty percent ice, and it belongs to Denmark.

su_that.trich: currently, an ice sheet covers about eighty percent of the island, restricting human activity largely to the coasts.

cau.chu: Greenland sits in the Arctic, and Norse settlers reached its southwest coast in nine eighty.

su_that.trich: Meanwhile, the Norse arrived and settled in the southern part of the island in 980.

cau.chu: In twelve sixty-one the Greenlanders accepted the overlordship of the King of Norway.

su_that.trich: In 1261 the population accepted the over lordship of the King of Norway, although it continued to have its own law.

cau.chu: In thirteen eighty Norway entered a personal union with Denmark, and Greenland came along.

su_that.trich: In 1380 the Norwegian kingdom entered into a personal union with the Kingdom of Denmark.

cau.chu: Denmark kept claiming the island for centuries, even with no contact with the settlers.

su_that.trich: Denmark–Norway, apparently believing the Norse settlements had survived, continued to claim sovereignty over the island despite the lack of any contact between the Norsemen

cau.chu: In seventeen twenty-one Denmark sent a missionary expedition to revive Christianity there.

su_that.trich: In 1721, aspiring to become a colonial power, Denmark-Norway sent a missionary expedition to Greenland with the stated aim of reinstating Christianity among descendants of the Norse Greenlanders

cau.chu: The missionaries found no Norse descendants, so they baptised the Inuit instead.

su_that.trich: When the missionaries found no descendants of the Norse Greenlanders, they baptised the Inuit they found living there instead.

cau.chu: Denmark then built trading colonies and imposed a trade monopoly on the coast.

su_that.trich: Denmark-Norway then developed trading colonies along the coast and imposed a trade monopoly and other colonial privileges on the area.

cau.chu: Then in eighteen fourteen came the twist, when the Treaty of Kiel handed Norway to Sweden.

su_that.trich: The Treaty of Kiel (Danish: Kieltraktaten) or Peace of Kiel

cau.chu: The treaty excluded Greenland, Iceland and the Faroes, which stayed with Denmark.

su_that.gia_tri: Greenland, Iceland and the Faroe Islands
su_that.trich: Specifically excluded from the exchange were the Norwegian dependencies of Greenland, Iceland and the Faroe Islands, which remained in the union with Denmark after being transferred.

cau.chu: Norway contested Danish Greenland in nineteen thirty-one, and lost at The Hague in nineteen thirty-three.

su_that.trich: Between 1931 and 1933, Norway contested the Danish possession of all of Greenland at the Permanent Court of International Justice in The Hague.
On 5 April 1933 however, the court ruled that on the basis of the Treaty of Kiel and subsequent treaties, Denmark was the sovereign over the whole of Greenland.

cau.chu: So a treaty about Norway is why this island flies Danish colors, but who signed it? That's part two.

su_that.trich: The treaty between the Kingdom of Denmark and the Kingdom of Sweden was negotiated by Danish diplomat Edmund Bourke (Burke) and Swedish envoy Baron Gustaf af Wetterstedt with British mediation.
